name: Timbe
sweep_summary: Timbe (timb1251) is not in the catalog. The single stress-title hit, Talić 2018 (NLLT), is a Glottolog mis-tag: its lingbuzz abstract and the Springer page show it concerns accent shift to proclitics in a Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian dialect and never mentions Timbe or PNG (Glottolog's Timbe bibliography is polluted with unrelated 'Upward...' titles). Beyond the listed item, I recovered the dead-linked Foster 1981 'Timbe Grammar Sketch' from the Wayback Machine (124 pp., image-only; saved and front matter scanned): it is a discourse-cohesion study with no phonology section and no stress statement. Suter's open 2018 Cologne thesis on Huon Peninsula comparative morphology was fetched sources and read; it has only reconstructive remarks (suffixes unstressed; presumed proto word accent on the verb-root initial syllable) and no Timbe word-stress statement, but its bibliography names the one phonological description, Foster & Foster 1972 'Timbe phonemics' (SIL Ukarumpa ms.), which is not online (SIL sites Cloudflare-403, OLAC/sealang unreachable from our machine) — highest acquisition priority. McElhanon 1967 (Oceanic Linguistics) is JSTOR-only, medium priority. No first-hand statement of Timbe word-stress placement was read; best_new_statement found=false.

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar (2018). Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages (Papua New Guinea). PhD thesis, University of Cologne. viii+331 pp. (Glottolog ref 577703)
sources.quote: The *u I reconstruct was not lowered in Borong, Somba, Kinalaknga and Kumukio, presumably because the suffix *-utup carried no primary stress. The majority of the reflexes point to *u as the vowel of the second syllable, too, and this vowel also failed to be lowered in Borong, Somba and Timbe. [...] The reason for the many irregular phonological developments in the nominal number suffixes is probably the fact that they are unstressed.
sources.locator: extracted text(Western Huon plural suffix, p. ~130); lines 7363-7368 (habitual suffix); no Timbe-specific stress passage
sources.note: Only incidental, reconstructive remarks: suffixes presumed unstressed; a presumed 'unitary word accent on the first syllable of the verb root' in Proto-Huon habitual forms. No synchronic statement of where Timbe word stress falls. Its bibliography is the best pointer to the unobtained Foster & Foster 1972 'Timbe phonemics'.

It is the likely home of a first-hand word-stress statement; whether it states one is unknown.
